s.en: Run tests through a TAP harness.

o.en: --verbose Print all test lines. Also sets TEST_VERBOSE
--lib Add 'lib' to the path for your tests (-Ilib).
--blib Add 'blib/lib' and 'blib/arch' to the path for your tests
--shuffle Run the tests in random order.
--color Colored test output (default). --nocolor Do not color test output. --count Show the X/Y test count when not verbose (default) --nocount Disable the X/Y test count.
--dry Dry run. Show test that would have run.
--failures Show failed tests.
--comments Show comments. --ignore-exit Ignore exit status from test scripts.
--merge Merge test scripts' STDERR with their STDOUT.
--recurse Recursively descend into directories. --reverse Run the tests in reverse order.
--quiet Suppress some test output while running tests.
--QUIET Only print summary results.

--parse Show full list of TAP parse errors, if any. --directives Only show results with TODO or SKIP directives. --timer Print elapsed time after each test. --trap Trap Ctrl-C and print summary on interrupt. --normalize Normalize TAP output in verbose output
Enable tainting checks.
Enable tainting warnings.
Enable fatal warnings.
Enable warnings.
--help Display this help
--version Display the version
--man Longer manpage for prove --norc Don't process default .proverc
Library paths to include.
Load plugin (searches App::Prove::Plugin::*.)
Load a module.

--exec Interpreter to run the tests ('' for compiled tests.) --ext Set the extension for tests (default '.t') --harness Define test harness to use. See TAP::Harness. --formatter Result formatter to use. See FORMATTERS. --source Load and/or configure a SourceHandler. See SOURCE HANDLERS.
--archive out.tgz Store the resulting TAP in an archive file.

--jobs N Run N test jobs in parallel (try 9.) --state=opts Control prove's persistent state. --statefile=file Use `file` instead of `.prove` for state --rc=rcfile Process options from rcfile --rules Rules for parallel vs sequential processing.

The "--rules" option is used to control which tests are run sequentially and which are run in parallel, if the "--jobs" option is specified. The option may be specified multiple times, and the order matters. The most practical use is likely to specify that some tests are not "parallel-ready".
